question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India added a new fundamental duty under Article 51-A?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Eighty-Sixth Amendment Act, 2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eighty-Sixth Amendment Act, 2002** added a new fundamental duty** under Article 51-A**.
 
• The Constitution of India's Eighty-sixth Amendment guarantees the right to education for children aged six to fourteen and early childhood care for children under the age of six.
 
• It has replaced Article 45 (Early Childhood Education) of directive principles of State policy with Article 21A (Right to Education as a Fundamental Right) and altered **Article 51A (Fundamental Duties)** to establish a new duty of parents to provide education to their children aged six to fourteen years.
 
• In part III of the constitution, the 86th Amendment Act of 2002 established the right to education as a fundamental right. "Who is a parent or guardian to provide chances for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the ages of six and fourteen years," was added after clause (J).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Constitution (88th Amendment) Act, 2003: **The Union and States collect and appropriate service taxes, which are levied by the Union. Articles 268, 270, and the VIIth Schedule are amended by the Act.
 
• The main goal of the** 85th Amendment Act of 2001 **was to extend the advantage of the reservation to SC/STs in areas of promotion and subsequent seniority.
